title: Map-cell classification decode: pick 1 of ~3,000 128 m tiles, confidence = softmax mass
hypothesis: The baseline fails for two coupled reasons visible in its metrics (coverage 1.0, false_fix_rate 1.0, p10 531 m): (1) sigmoid+MSE direct regression of (u,v) through a global-average-pooled feature is a mean-seeking objective — under ambiguity it interpolates toward the map centre instead of committing to a place, which is structurally wrong for a memorization task; (2) its confidence head is trained on 'error < half the map extent', a target that is always satisfied, so it confidently emits every guess and the mission score sits at the confidently-wrong-everywhere ceiling of 2.0. Reparameterizing localization as classification over a grid of 128 m map cells attacks both at once: cross-entropy over cells is multimodal and memorization-friendly (each cell gets its own logit — no averaging between competing hypotheses), and the softmax distribution is an intrinsic honesty signal — when belief is spread across many tiles the max probability drops below the scorer's 0.3 threshold and the frame becomes a safe abstention instead of a false fix. The cell size is chosen so the parameterization alone suffices: a 128 m cell's half-diagonal is 90.5 m < the 100 m usable radius, so a correctly classified cell centre is already a usable fix, with a small offset head adding margin.
method: One change: replace the regression head/decode in model/model.py with a map-cell classification head plus within-cell offset, decoded inside the exported ONNX graph (argmax over cell logits -> gather precomputed cell-centre table -> add offset), with conf = max softmax probability; model/train.py switches the loss to cross-entropy on the centre cell + smooth-L1 on the within-cell offset, and resamples a fresh 6,000-crop lattice subset with fresh rotation angles each epoch (a coverage precondition of the mechanism: 2,970 cells cannot be covered by one fixed 6,000-crop draw, but 8 fresh draws see ~48k distinct vantages, ~16 per cell). No other stage changes; harness CLI and its 6000/8 budget respected as-is.
expected_outcome: mission_score drops from 2.00075 to <= 1.2, target < 1.0. Mechanically: usable_fix_rate rises from 0.0 to >= 0.25 (every correctly-classified confident cell is within 90.5 m by construction), false_fix_rate falls from 1.0 to <= 0.6 because low-softmax frames become abstentions rather than false fixes. Even the pessimistic outcome (model abstains heavily but keeps coverage >= 0.2 with decent accuracy on its confident subset) lands near 1.0, still a large improvement over 2.0. Standing metric check: the improvement must show up in usable_fix_rate itself, not only in the score. Residual risks, in order: coverage collapse below 0.2 (softmax never exceeds 0.3 -> FAIL 1e9; mitigated by light label smoothing only, 0.05, so a memorized cell can still reach ~0.95) and adjacent-cell confusion at cell borders (a near-miss into the neighbouring cell is a false fix; the offset head plus label-free CE sharpness should keep this bounded).
eli5: The old model answered 'where is this photo?' by guessing two GPS numbers directly — and when unsure, that kind of guess drifts toward the middle of the map, which is confidently wrong almost everywhere. The new model works like a mail sorter instead: Berlin is cut into about 3,000 postcode-sized tiles, and the model picks which tile the photo belongs to, then fine-tunes the spot inside it. The tiles are sized so that naming the right tile already counts as a good fix. Best of all, a multiple-choice answer comes with built-in honesty: if the model's belief is smeared across many tiles, its top choice scores low and the drone simply says 'not sure' and waits for the next frame — which is far safer than pointing at the wrong street with full confidence.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (widened last layer to 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the chosen tile's centre to the exact spot inside it

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile; belief smeared across tiles means low confidence, so the drone abstains instead of taking a false fix

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: cross-entropy on the true tile + offset loss; each epoch redraws a fresh random 6,000-view sample of the full Berlin lattice with fresh rotations, so all tiles get covered over training

implementation_brief:
Rewrite the model head/decode in model/model.py and the loss/sampling in model/train.py. Everything under pipeline/ is FROZEN — read it, never edit it.

=== FIXED CONTRACTS (restated — the frozen scorer depends on these) ===
1. train.py CLI must remain: python -m model.train --area <name> --out-dir <dir> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N] [--seed N]. The harness calls it with --epochs 8 --max-crops-per-bucket 6000. Keep appending a per-area info dict to <out-dir>/train_info.json (list of dicts) and writing the ONNX to <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx.
2. ONNX export contract (model/model.py docstring): one ONNX per area taking a 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] (input name 'frame') and returning [[u, v, conf]] — u, v normalized map coords in [0,1] relative to meta width/height, conf in [0,1]. Export with opset_version=17, dynamo=False. The DECODE MUST LIVE INSIDE THE GRAPH: the scorer runs the ONNX directly (pipeline/score.py predict()) and reads u, v, conf from the single output.
3. Gates: exported ONNX <= 4 MiB, single-thread host CPU latency <= 250 ms (baseline was 0.59 ms; this design stays comfortably under).
4. Keep estimate_position(frame, onnx_path, meta) in model/model.py working unchanged (it only runs the ONNX and converts px->lonlat; no edits needed beyond leaving it intact).

=== model/model.py ===
GRID: CELL_PX = 128. Grid dims from the area's meta: gw = ceil(meta['width']/CELL_PX), gh = ceil(meta['height']/CELL_PX), C = gw*gh (Berlin: 55*54 = 2970). build_model must therefore take meta: change the signature to build_model(meta) and construct the net with (gw, gh, width, height) baked in.

CLASS CellLocNet(nn.Module), replacing TinyLocNet:
- Trunk: same strided conv pattern as the baseline (Conv3x3 stride2 + BN + ReLU) with chans [3, 32, 64, 128, 160], then global average pool -> 160-d feature. (~277k trunk params.)
- Heads: logits = Linear(160, C); offset = Linear(160, 2), passed through tanh and scaled by 0.5 so offsets live in (-0.5, 0.5) cell units.
- Constant tables registered as buffers (they become ONNX constants): cell_u[C], cell_v[C], float32, where for cell index i: cell_u[i] = ((i % gw) + 0.5) * CELL_PX / width, cell_v[i] = ((i // gw) + 0.5) * CELL_PX / height. Also store scale_u = CELL_PX / width, scale_v = CELL_PX / height as buffers or Python floats baked into the graph.
- forward(x) returns TRAINING outputs as a tuple (logits [B,C], offset [B,2]) when self.training is True, but for export/eval the module's forward must produce the deployed decode. Cleanest pattern: put the trunk+heads in forward_features(), and make forward(x) always compute the DEPLOYED decode: p = softmax(logits, dim=1); conf, idx = p.max(dim=1) (torch.max returns both); u = cell_u.index_select(0, idx) + offset[:,0]*scale_u; v = cell_v.index_select(0, idx) + offset[:,1]*scale_v; clamp u and v to [0,1]; return torch.stack([u, v, conf], dim=1) -> shape [B,3]. Give the module a separate method training_outputs(x) -> (logits, offset) that train.py calls explicitly; forward() stays the pure deployed path so export_onnx works on forward unchanged. (index_select on a buffer + max + softmax all export fine under opset 17 legacy exporter; do NOT use fancy indexing like cell_u[idx].)
- Param budget check: trunk ~277k + logits head 160*2970+2970 ~= 478k + offset head 322 -> ~756k params ~= 3.0 MiB fp32 ONNX. Under the 4 MiB gate; do not widen further.
- loss_fn: replace with loss_fn(logits, offset_pred, target_cell_idx, target_offset): F.cross_entropy(logits, target_cell_idx, label_smoothing=0.05) + 1.0 * F.smooth_l1_loss(offset_pred, target_offset). No confidence loss term exists any more — confidence IS the softmax max; delete the old BCE machinery.
- export_onnx(model, path): unchanged mechanics (dummy 1x3x128x128, input_names=['frame'], output_names=['uvc'], opset 17, dynamo=False). model.eval() first so forward() is the deployed decode.
- Update the module docstring to describe the cell-classification contract; keep the two bullet contract lines intact.

=== model/train.py ===
- load_training_tensors -> replace with a per-epoch sampler. Keep loading meta and the single 'asis' relight image once (LIGHTING_BUCKETS has exactly one entry on this branch; keep iterating LIGHTING_BUCKETS rather than hardcoding 'asis'). Enumerate the full train lattice once: crops = list_crops(area, meta['width'], meta['height'], 'train').
- EACH EPOCH: draw a fresh random subset of max_crops_per_bucket crop records (rng.choice without replacement), extract each with a fresh random angle float(rng.uniform(0,360)) via extract_crop, and build the batch tensors for that epoch only. This replaces the baseline's extract-once-reuse-every-epoch scheme and is deliberate: over 8 epochs the model sees ~48k distinct (position, rotation) vantages, ~16 per cell, which is the coverage the 2,970-way classification needs. Extraction of 6,000 crops takes tens of seconds per epoch — acceptable; keep it single-process, no DataLoader machinery.
- Targets per crop (raster px centre cx, cy; CELL_PX and gw from the model/meta): target_cell_idx = (cy // CELL_PX) * gw + (cx // CELL_PX) as int64; target_offset = float32 pair ((cx % CELL_PX)/CELL_PX - 0.5, (cy % CELL_PX)/CELL_PX - 0.5), matching the (-0.5,0.5) cell-unit convention of the offset head.
- Training step: model.train(); logits, off = model.training_outputs(xb); loss = loss_fn(logits, off, cell_idx_b, off_b). Keep Adam lr=1e-3, batch 64, seed handling, device selection (mps/cuda/cpu) exactly as now.
- build_model(meta) call site: pass the loaded meta. Export path, train_info.json append, and the printed JSON stay as-is; keep 'init': 'from-scratch' and add 'n_cells': C and 'distinct_vantages_seen': epochs*max_crops_per_bucket to the info dict for the record.
- crop_center_norm is no longer needed for targets; drop its import if unused.

=== What must NOT change ===
Anything in pipeline/ (frozen), the CLI flags and their meanings, the ONNX input/output names and shapes, the output file locations, opset/dynamo settings, and the single-model-per-area structure. Do not add new CLI flags. Do not touch loop.sh or the scorer. No pretrained weights (init stays from-scratch).
